name: Caius Oluwafemi-Strand
description: The foundational figure of neural-feed performance, Caius Oluwafemi-Strand was among the first generation of performers to train specifically for full-sensory immersion rather than adapting from flat-screen or holographic technique. Now in his seventies and formally retired since 2218, he spent thirty-five years defining what neural-feed acting could be — a body of work so foundational that contemporary performers are still taught his method, though Vantablack owns the licensing rights to the methodology itself. He has become increasingly critical of the industry he built.
cultural_impact: He is the unavoidable origin point of neural-feed performance as a discipline; every conversation about the form, whether celebratory or critical, begins with his work.
story_hooks: Oluwafemi-Strand claims to have documented evidence of Vantablack's unauthorized modifications to his methodology — evidence stored in physical format he cannot safely access.
A young performer is experiencing the neural degradation he described in his underground interview; she wants him to testify on her behalf, but his own contract may prevent it.
He is quietly mentoring an underground director, providing technical knowledge that Vantablack considers proprietary — a situation that could destroy both of them if exposed.
